brief.text: Plan a car assembly plant that builds 30 compact electric cars an hour. Start from steel coils and finish with cars driving off the line: stamping, body shop with welding robots, paint shop, general assembly with battery and motor marriage, and final inspection. Use conveyors throughout.

requirements.name: Compact EV Assembly Plant
requirements.summary: Automated 30 JPH compact electric vehicle assembly plant transforming steel coils into finished cars across stamping, body shop, paint shop, general assembly, and final inspection.
assumptions: Floor size set to 180 m by 120 m (21,600 m2), approximately six times the 3,538 m2 total equipment footprint to accommodate aisles and conveyor runs.
Receiving dock placed on the west wall (W) and finished vehicle exit dock on the east wall (E) for linear west-to-east material flow.
Main electrical switchgear placed on the north wall (N) and process water supply on the south wall (S).
Parallel station counts sized by 30 JPH takt time at 85% utilization; slow continuous processes such as E-coat dip, spray booths, and curing ovens use multi-minute per-body cycle times.

research.summary:
WORKING NOTES: 30 JPH COMPACT EV ASSEMBLY PLANT
Target output: 30 vehicles/hour (120 s takt time), approx. 150,000 vehicles/year (estimate, 2-3 shifts).
Estimated plant floor area: 200,000-250,000 m2 (scaled from 185,000 m2 for a 75,000/year plant).

1. STAMPING
Process steps: Coil uncoiling/blanking, drawing, trimming/piercing, flanging/hemming.
Equipment: Coil straightener/feeder, 4-6 press tandem or servo press line, inter-press robotic arms.
Cycle time: 4-5 s/stroke (12-15 strokes/min) on automated tandem lines; 2.6-3.75 s/stroke (16-23 SPM) on servo lines.
Single-station footprint: 10 x 8 m per large press (estimate).
Power draw: 300-500 kW per heavy 2,000-ton automotive press (estimate; smaller 300-550 ton presses draw 55-75 kW).

2. BODY SHOP
Process steps: Underbody assembly, body-side framing, body-in-white (BIW) roof/main framing, closure hanging.
Equipment: 6- and 7-axis spot welding robots (~5,000 spot welds/car), MIG/laser welders, clamping fixtures.
Cycle time: 120 s/station (1-3 s per spot weld).
Single-station footprint: 8 x 6 m per dual-robot cell (estimate).
Power draw: ~60 kW peak per welding robot; 120-240 kW per multi-robot station (estimate).

3. PAINT SHOP
Process steps: Pretreatment and E-coat dip, seam sealing, 4-wet primer/basecoat/clearcoat, curing ovens.
Equipment: Immersion tanks, conditioned spray booths with 6-axis paint robots, electric/gas curing ovens, exhaust oxidizers.
Cycle time: 120 s/station (estimate, matching plant takt; ovens hold multiple bodies continuously).
Single-station footprint: 12 x 6 m per booth station (estimate; paint shop uses ~1/3 of plant area).
Power draw: 8-10 MW total shop electrical load (fans up to 4 MW), ~245 kWh/vehicle; 200-400 kW per booth/oven zone (estimate).

4. GENERAL ASSEMBLY
Process steps: Trim line (wiring, dash, glass), EV battery pack and motor marriage, final line (seats, wheels, fluids).
Equipment: Skillet conveyors, overhead carriers, chassis-marriage AGVs with 2,500 kg synchronized electric lifts, DC torque tools.
Cycle time: 120 s/station (estimate, matching plant takt).
Single-station footprint: 8 x 5 m (estimate).
Power draw: 20-50 kW/station (estimate).

5. FINAL INSPECTION (END-OF-LINE)
Process steps: HV/ADAS electronic diagnostics, wheel alignment and headlamp aim, roller brake and chassis dyno test, water-leak test, visual check.
Equipment: EOL diagnostic rigs, roller brake tester, chassis dynamometer, alignment sensors, water booth.
Cycle time: 120 s/station (estimate, matching plant takt).
Single-station footprint: 10 x 5 m per bay (estimate).
Power draw: 50-100 kW per dyno/test bay (estimate).

MATERIAL MOVEMENT BETWEEN STEPS
Stamping to Body Shop: Forklifts/AGVs with part racks (estimate).
Body Shop to Paint Shop to General Assembly: Overhead power-and-free monorail carriers.
Within General Assembly: Skillet/slat floor conveyors for trim/final; line-guided or inertial AGVs for battery/motor marriage.
Final Inspection: Driven on own wheels off the line.
